items.headline: U.S. prepares Monday Iran sanctions announcement as Hormuz remains virtually stalled
items.category: Geopolitics / Energy / Inflation / China / Capital Allocation
items.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is scheduled to detail a new Iran sanctions package on 24 August at 2 p.m. EDT after describing the planned measures as the toughest yet. Iran remains defiant, unauthorized oil tanker traffic through Hormuz is still near a standstill, and Washington is explicitly seeking cooperation from China, the largest buyer of shipped Iranian oil.
items.whyItMatters: The risk has moved from a general sanctions threat to an imminent policy event with potential secondary-sanctions exposure. AGCI treats Monday as a binary catalyst for oil, inflation expectations, Chinese risk assets, freight, insurance and long-duration multiples.
items.agciSignal: MONDAY SANCTIONS CATALYST / SECONDARY-SANCTIONS TAIL / KEEP ENERGY-INFLATION HEDGE

items.headline: Nvidia-linked AI server prices reportedly set to rise more than 15% as memory costs surge
items.summary: A Bloomberg report cited by Reuters says some of Nvidia's largest customers have been told that prices for AI servers using Nvidia chips will rise by more than 15% in many cases for systems shipping in early 2027, driven primarily by higher memory costs. Reuters had not independently verified the report and Nvidia had not commented at publication time.
items.whyItMatters: This is a material cost-of-capacity signal ahead of Nvidia's 26 August earnings. Higher server pricing can support semiconductor and memory pricing power, but it also raises the all-in hurdle rate for hyperscaler AI projects and increases the importance of utilization, monetization and FCF discipline.
items.agciSignal: AI COST CURVE MOVES HIGHER / PRICING POWER VS ROI TEST / DO NOT CHASE BEFORE EARNINGS

items.headline: Sinopec profit rises despite Hormuz shock, while weak fuel and chemicals demand persists
items.summary: Sinopec reported first-half net profit up 19.3% year over year to 25.63 billion yuan despite lower crude throughput and a 16 billion yuan inventory impairment. Refining margin improved 44.1% as the company diversified crude sourcing, managed purchase timing and optimized product mix; domestic refined-product and chemicals demand remained weak.
items.whyItMatters: The result shows that sophisticated refiners can defend margins during the Hormuz shock, but it also confirms softer Chinese end-demand and the scale of working-capital and inventory volatility created by geopolitical oil disruption.
items.agciSignal: REFINING RESILIENCE / CHINA DEMAND STILL SOFT / OIL VOLATILITY REMAINS EARNINGS-RISK

items.headline: Greed holds at 87 while valuation stays at 85 and EUPHORIA_RISK remains active
items.summary: The 23 August AGCI snapshot keeps Greed at 87/100 and Valuation at 85/100. Regime remains Mid Bull, confidence is 72/100, one-day Greed change is zero and the matrix remains EUPHORIA_RISK — Capital preservation / Do not chase.
items.whyItMatters: Weekend news has not produced a valuation reset. With both psychology and valuation still extreme, new geopolitical and AI-cost catalysts should be treated as reasons to preserve optionality rather than increase broad market beta.
items.agciSignal: EXTREME GREED + EXTREME VALUATION / NO RESET / PRESERVE LIQUIDITY
